A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ItemizedCLIP work and contain complete main text and supplementary Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ItemizedCLIP classification, retrieval, segmentation, ablation and qualitative results across medical imaging, remote sensing and natural images.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, ILA with UWP and masking, IIS, MPS, KTA, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The domain-specific coefficient revision in Table 12 changes a reported experimental setting, not the proposed method formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five training domains and evaluation datasets, including the medical classification benchmarks, RSICD, MSCOCO/Flickr retrieval and BraTS2021 segmentation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding main-text and appendix comparisons retain the same baselines, including Prima, FullViT, HLIP, the CT foundation models, CLIP/SigLIP, DreamLIP and FLAIR. No comparator is added, removed or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Appendix Table 12 changes the remote-sensing UWP upweighting factor from 1.5 to 2. Other reported settings remain unchanged. This is a limited revision to the stated training protocol; neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, HLIP-SN and normal-check comparisons, diverse-sampling analysis, completeness analysis and qualitative retrieval/attention examples are retained. Relocating their displays does not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Reporting of task-averaged metrics remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Result entries in Tables 2–11 and 13–16, plotted results and qualitative examples remain unchanged after matching relocations. For example, UM220K mean AUC remains 90.5 and full-model BraTS2021 mIoU remains 17.5. Table 12's changed number is a hyperparameter, not a result.

T1.justification: The loss equations, similarity definitions, attention-map similarity metric and Mean Lowest Logit definition are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: itemized supervision, representations enforcing independence and completeness, and empirical performance and interpretability across five domains.

C2.justification: Interpretations of IIS, UWP and diverse sampling, and limitations concerning scale, compute and text quality are retained. Section 5.6 rephrases the same claim that strong segmentation requires both IIS and MPS.

D1.justification: Table 12 revises the documented remote-sensing UWP factor from 1.5 to 2, changing information needed for reproduction. Implementation descriptions, preprocessing, prompts, hardware, training times and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A remain unchanged. References 24 and 40 receive publication-metadata updates for the same works, rather than introducing new literature.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar, punctuation and quotation-mark edits, rephrases several sentences and updates bibliographic metadata. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 7 and 8 move from page 7 to page 8, Table 9 moves from page 8 to page 9, and appendix Tables 10–11 shift placement. Spacing and text flow change, while the same figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence and limitations remain effectively unchanged. Local copyediting, refreshed references and table relocation provide limited presentation changes. The unexplained UWP coefficient revision is not accompanied by evidence establishing improved experimental validity, so the revision does not demonstrate a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
